components.name: alert
components.title: Alert
components.purpose: A message inside a view about the state of what the view shows.
whenToUse: To tell the reader something about the run, task or repository on screen that changes what they should do next.
To report the result of an action where it happened, when the result should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For a mistake in one form control. Use the field's error message.
When a whole view failed to load. Use an error state.
When a view has nothing to show yet. Use an empty state.
For a confirmation that should go away by itself. Use a toast.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Context the reader may want. Label it Note.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Something finished as intended. Label it Done.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Something will go wrong unless the reader acts. Label it Warning.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Something failed. Label it Error, and say what to do about it.

accessibility: Every alert holds a gw-alert__label naming its tone in a word. The stylesheet draws the matching icon, so tone is carried by a word, an icon and a colour.
An alert that is part of the view when it loads takes no role. It is read in order with the rest of the content.
An alert the app adds in response to something takes role="status" for info, success and warning, which is announced when the screen reader is next idle.
Use role="alert" only for a failure the reader must know about now. It interrupts whatever is being read.
For the announcement to be reliable, add the element with its role first, or keep it in the page empty and hidden with the hidden attribute, then fill in the text.
The title and body are paragraphs, not headings, so an alert does not change the outline of the view.
At most one action: a gw-button gw-button--small inside gw-alert__action. Never primary. Use a link element when it goes to another view.
Do not move focus to an alert. The role announces it.

components.name: app-header
components.title: App header
components.purpose: The top bar of an app: the product name or the current view's title, with an optional back link, actions and a tray for approvals that are waiting.
whenToUse: Once per screen, as the first thing in the page.
With the product name on a top-level screen, and with a back link and the view's title on a screen below one.
With the tray when something, such as an approval, must stay in sight on every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a view's title with its description and main action inside the page. Use a page header.
For moving between the main destinations on a phone. Use a tab bar.
For a message about the state of the app, such as a lost connection. Use a banner under the header.
For the main action of a view. Put a primary button in the view, never in the header.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Scrolls away with the page. Use it when the screen is short or the header holds nothing the reader needs while scrolling.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Stays at the top while the page scrolls. Use it when the back link, the actions or the tray must stay in reach.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: One row, 52px tall, with 44px controls, at every width. The tray adds a row below it only while it holds something.

accessibility: Use a header element. Outside main it is the page's banner landmark, so a page has one.
The product name is a link to the first screen. The view title is the page's h1 when the header shows one.
The back link names where it goes: visible text such as Tasks, or aria-label="Back to tasks" when it is only the icon.
An icon-only action has an aria-label that says what it does and to what, such as Search tasks. Its icon carries aria-hidden="true".
Use a link for an action that goes to another view and a button for one that acts on this view.
Tab moves through the name or back link, then the actions, then the tray, in the order they are written. Enter follows a link, and Enter or Space presses a button.
A long title is cut with an ellipsis. Keep the full title in the document title or in the page, where it can be read whole.
An empty tray takes no space and is not announced. Leave the element in place and fill it when something is waiting.
With the sticky variant, give the scrolling container scroll-padding-top of the header's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.

components.name: approval
components.title: Approval
components.purpose: One request from an agent that waits for the reader's answer: what would run, where, for whom and why, with Allow and Decline.
whenToUse: When an agent is blocked until the reader allows or declines a tool call or a command.
Alone in a view for one request, or as list items in a queue of several.
whenNotToUse: For a request that was already answered or denied. Use a message row in the transcript.
To say how many requests wait. Use the pending tray.
To confirm an action the reader started themselves, such as deleting a workspace. Use a dialog.

variants.name: normal
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The risk line reads Normal risk and what keeps it so, beside an info icon.

variants.name: elevated
variants.use: A request that reaches outside the task's worktree, deletes, or cannot be undone. The risk line reads Elevated risk and why, beside a warning icon, on a tinted band.

accessibility: Use an article with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-approval__title, a heading at the level the view needs. The title says who asks and for what.

Emphasis: when a view shows a single approval, Allow may be the view's primary action, gw-button gw-button--primary. When approvals are listed, each card sits in its own li of a ul and Allow is a plain gw-button, never primary, so a queue has no competing primary actions.

Allow comes first and Decline sits at the far end of gw-approval__actions. Both are always visible, carry data-gw-critical so the checker can see they are never hidden, and are never placed inside a details element.
The risk line always starts with the words Normal risk or Elevated risk and then says why. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so the tone is never colour alone.
gw-approval__command holds exactly what would run, as text, with characters that cannot be seen written out. It wraps, and never scrolls sideways.
Supporting detail goes in a details element with a text summary, such as Show the full request. It holds no control the reader needs in order to answer.

A note on declining is optional. Under the actions, add a details element whose summary reads Decline with a note, holding a labelled field and its own button, Decline and send note. It starts closed, without the open attribute, and the plain Decline above it still declines with no note.

While the answer is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the pressed button, change its label to Allowing or Declining, and disable the other. If sending fails, restore both and add gw-approval__error with role="alert", saying that nothing was allowed.

Tab reaches the summary, then Allow, then Decline. Enter and Space activate each. The component needs no script: the app sets aria-busy and disabled, and removes the card once the request is answered. Move focus to the next card or the view's heading when it goes.

components.name: badge
components.title: Badge
components.purpose: A status in a word or two, such as a task's station.
whenToUse: For the one status of an item that the reader acts on or scans for: Building, Awaiting decision, Blocked.
Once per row of a list or table, as the row's trailing element.
Once beside the title of a view, for the status of the thing the view shows.
whenNotToUse: For facts that are not a status, such as a repository, a branch, a count or a time. Write them as plain text.
For several statuses on one item. Pick the one the reader acts on and write the rest as text. Eight or more badges outside list rows in one view fail the excess-badges rule.
For something the reader can press. Use a button or a link.
For a message with a sentence in it. Use a banner or an inline message.
As a count on an icon. Write the count as text next to a label.

variants.name: neutral
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. A status that needs nothing from the reader yet: Queued, Draft.

variants.name: info
variants.use: Work in progress that needs nothing from the reader: Building, Verifying, Reviewing.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Finished as intended: Decided, Merged, Tests passed.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Waiting on the reader or on something outside the task: Awaiting decision, Blocked.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Stopped or failed: Interrupted, Failed.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 24px tall with 12px text. It fits a dense list row without making it taller.

accessibility: Use a span. The badge is text, and a screen reader reads its words in place.
The words carry the status. The tone only supports them, so never rely on the colour, and never use a badge with an icon and no text.
An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". Use the same icon for the same status everywhere.
Write the status in sentence case, in one to three words, in the same words everywhere the status appears.
A badge is not focusable and takes no press. When a status changes while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the badge.

components.name: banner
components.title: Banner
components.purpose: One message about the state of the whole app, across the full width under the app header.
whenToUse: For a condition that affects every screen and is still true, such as a lost connection, a paused agent host or a session about to end.
Directly under the app header, across the full width, for as long as the condition lasts.
With one action when there is one thing the reader can do about it, such as Retry.
whenNotToUse: For the result of something the reader just did, such as Task saved. Confirm it where it happened, or use a toast.
For a problem with one field or one form. Use the field's error message.
For a problem with one item in a view, such as a failed run. Show it on that item.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.
For more than one message at a time. Show the most severe one.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Something the reader should know that needs no action, such as a planned restart or a restored connection. Set role="status".

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Something is degraded or about to go wrong and the app is still usable, such as Reconnecting. Set role="status".

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Something has failed and work is blocked until it is fixed. Set role="alert".

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: At least 44px tall and as wide as its container. The text wraps, and on a narrow screen the action and the dismiss button move below it.

accessibility: Set role="status" on an info or warning banner, so a screen reader announces it when the reader pauses. Set role="alert" on a danger banner, so it is announced at once.
Keep the banner element in the page and change its text, or add the banner with its text already in it. Either way the message is announced once.

Do not set aria-busy on the banner. A screen reader holds back the announcement of a busy region. While the action runs, set aria-busy="true" on the action button and change its label, such as Retrying.
The stylesheet draws the tone's icon, so the tone never depends on colour and needs no markup. The text carries the whole message.

The action and the dismiss button sit together in a gw-banner__actions element after the text. The action is one gw-button gw-button--small, with a label that says what it does. Do not make it primary.
The dismiss button is a button with aria-label="Dismiss", and its icon carries aria-hidden="true". Offer it only when the message is safe to lose. When it is pressed, move focus to the main content.
Tab reaches the action and then the dismiss button, in that order. Enter and Space press them.
The banner does not take focus when it appears, so it never interrupts typing.

components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.purpose: An action the reader takes on the current view.
whenToUse: To start, save, confirm or cancel something on the current view.
To submit a form.
whenNotToUse: To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
For an action repeated on every row of a list. Give that one secondary or quiet emphasis, never primary.
As a second primary action in the same view. A view has one.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Any action that is not the main one.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The one main action of a view, dialog or popover.

variants.name: quiet
variants.use: A minor action that should not draw the eye, such as Cancel or View log.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: An action that deletes or cannot be undone. The label names what is lost.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. Use it unless the button sits in a dense row.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: Drawn 32px tall for dense rows and toolbars. Its pointer target is still 44px.

accessibility: Use a button element, with type="button" unless it submits a form.
The label is a verb and what it acts on, such as Start task. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
Set the disabled attribute when the action is unavailable. A disabled button leaves the tab order.
Use aria-disabled="true" instead only when the button must stay focusable so its reason can be read. The app then ignores presses.
Set aria-busy="true" while the action runs, change the label to say what is happening, and ignore further presses.
Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.

components.name: code-block
components.title: Code block
components.purpose: A block of mono text for a command, a log or a program's output.
whenToUse: For a command the reader may copy, the output of a command, a log, or an excerpt of a file.
With the scroll variant when columns must stay aligned, such as a table printed by a tool.
With line numbers when the text refers to lines of a file.
whenNotToUse: For a change to a file. Use the diff.
For a word or a path inside a sentence. Use a code element in the running text.
For a value the reader edits. Use a field.
For prose, or to make a message look technical. Mono text is for text a machine wrote or will read.

variants.name: wrapping
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Long lines wrap at any character, so nothing is hidden at phone width.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: Lines keep their length and the body scrolls sideways inside the block. Set tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label on the body.

accessibility: Use a figure holding a pre with a code element inside it. An optional figcaption with the class gw-code-block__caption names what ran or which file it is, and comes first.

With the scroll variant, give the pre tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label that says what it holds. It can then take focus, and the arrow keys scroll it. Leave all three off a wrapping block, which never scrolls.

For line numbers, give the code element the class gw-code-block__lines and write each line as a gw-code-block__line span holding a gw-code-block__number span and a gw-code-block__text span. The numbers are real text, so a screen reader reads them, and they are left out of a copy.
Write the text exactly as the tool printed it. Escape the characters <, > and & in markup.
When there is no output, keep the caption and replace the pre with a gw-code-block__note paragraph that says so in a sentence. Never show an empty box.
Colour carries no meaning inside a block. A failure is said in the output's own words or in text beside the block.

components.name: composer
components.title: Composer
components.purpose: The prompt input under a transcript: a textarea that grows with its content, and Send.
whenToUse: At the bottom of a transcript, to send the next prompt to the agent.
To stop a running turn from the same place the reader sends from.
whenNotToUse: For one line of text in a form, such as a task title. Use a field.
For longer text that is saved with a form and not sent as a message. Use a textarea.
To answer an approval request. Use the approval's own Allow and Decline.

variants.name: default
variants.use: In the flow of the page, as wide as its container.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Held to the bottom of the scrolling view, with a top border, its own padding and room for the home indicator. whenToUse: To show what a task changed in one file, before the reader decides on it.
One diff per file. For several files, list them and put each diff in a row disclosure.
The counts alone, gw-diff__counts, beside a file's name in a list row or a disclosure summary.

components.name: disclosure
components.title: Disclosure
components.purpose: A native details element that shows or hides detail under a summary written in text.
whenToUse: For detail most readers can do without: a log, the environment, the steps of a finished attempt.
With the row variant inside a list row, for a changed file that opens to its diff. The summary holds the path and the counts.
For the one group of advanced settings in a view. Mark that details element with data-gw-advanced.
whenNotToUse: For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical that can be reached only inside closed content fails the hidden-critical-action rule: show it in the view too, or open the disclosure by default.
Nested more than two levels. A third level fails the disclosure-depth rule: move that content to a view of its own.
With a summary that is only an icon or is empty. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule.
For a list of actions that opens over the page. Use a menu.
For sections where opening one must close the others. This component has no script, so each disclosure opens and closes alone.

Tab reaches the summary. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order and is skipped by a screen reader, and the browser's find-in-page opens it.
Set the open attribute in markup to start open. Start open when the content holds an action the reader needs.
Fetch heavy content, such as a diff, when the disclosure opens, and show the content's own loading state until it arrives.

The app sets nothing but the open attribute, which the browser manages.

components.name: page-header
components.title: Page header
components.purpose: The top of a view: its title, an optional one-line description and the view's one optional primary action.
whenToUse: Once, at the top of a view's content, to say what the view is.
With the action when the view has one main thing to do, such as New task on the task list.
In the compact variant above a board, a transcript or a diff, where the content needs the height.
whenNotToUse: For the bar across the top of the app with the product name and the back link. Use an app header.
For the heading of a section inside a view. Use a plain h2.
For a second or third action. Put those in the view as secondary buttons, or behind a menu.
For help text of more than a line. Put it in the view or link to the documentation.

variants.name: default

variants.name: compact
variants.use: The title at 16px with a 12px description, for a dense screen. Pair it with a small button.

accessibility: Use a header element, with the title as the page's h1. When the app header already shows the view title as the h1, leave the page header out.
The description is a p directly after the title, one sentence long.
The action is one button, or one link styled as a button when it goes to another view. It may be the view's primary button, and then no other button in the view is primary.
In the compact variant use gw-button--small, which keeps a 44px pointer target.
On a narrow screen the action moves below the text instead of squeezing it. A long title wraps and is never cut.
The header adds no keyboard behaviour. Tab reaches the action in document order, after the title and description.

components.name: pending-tray
components.title: Pending tray
components.purpose: How many approvals are waiting for the reader, in words and a count, linking to the queue from every screen.
whenToUse: In the trailing slot of the app header, on every signed-in screen, so a waiting approval is never out of sight.
As the one way from any screen to the approval queue.
whenNotToUse: To show the request itself or to answer it. Use an approval.
For a count of anything the reader does not have to act on, such as open tasks. Write that as plain text.
As a navigation item for the queue screen. Use the app's navigation, and keep the tray as well.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The link is drawn 32px tall to fit a header row. Its pointer target is still 44px.

accessibility: The block is a div with aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true". Keep it in the page on every screen and change only what it holds, so a screen reader announces the new sentence when the count changes without moving focus.

While approvals wait, it holds one link, gw-pending-tray__link, to the queue. The link text is the whole sentence: the count in gw-pending-tray__count, then approval waiting or approvals waiting. Never show the count alone.
The filled box around the count is decoration. The sentence carries the meaning, so the count is never colour alone.

When nothing waits, either leave the block empty, which hides the tray and keeps the live region, or show gw-pending-tray__text reading No approvals waiting. Use the same quiet text while the count is loading and when it could not be read, and say which in words.
The link is reached with Tab and followed with Enter. The app sets the count, the wording and the link's href, and nothing else.

components.name: select
components.title: Select
components.purpose: A native select as the control of a field, for one choice from a short fixed list.
whenToUse: For one choice from a list the app already knows: a base branch, a repository, a model.
When the list is too long to show as radio buttons, from about five options up.
whenNotToUse: For two to four options the reader should compare. Use a radio group.
For on or off. Use a checkbox.
For a list long enough to need searching, or for free text. Use a text input in a field.
For a menu of actions. Use buttons.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as the field. Limit the width on the field's container.

accessibility: Use a select element carrying both gw-field__control and gw-select__control, wrapped in an element with gw-select, inside gw-field. The wrapper only draws the chevron.
Give it a label element whose for attribute matches the select's id.
When nothing is chosen yet, make the first option an instruction with an empty value, such as Choose a repository, and set required on the select.
For an invalid choice, set aria-invalid="true" on the select and link a gw-field__error that says what to choose.
While the options load, set disabled, show one option that says what is loading, and say what is being fetched in the description. Remove disabled when the options arrive.
The keyboard is the browser's own: Space or Enter opens the list, the arrow keys move, typing jumps to a matching option, Escape closes.
The chevron is decoration drawn by the stylesheet. It needs no markup and takes no pointer events.

components.name: spinner
components.title: Spinner
components.purpose: A sign that something is in progress when how long it will take is not known.
whenToUse: While a view or part of one loads and nothing can be shown yet.
While a background step runs, such as cloning a repository or running tests, beside the name of the step.
whenNotToUse: Inside a button that is working. Set aria-busy="true" on the button, which draws its own.
When the amount done is known. Use a progress element.
When the shape of the content is known and it will arrive within a moment. Show the layout with its text missing, not a spinner.
For anything that takes less than about a second. Show nothing.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: A 16px mark with text at the interface size. Inside a list, a panel or a row.

sizes.name: large
sizes.use: A 24px mark with 16px text. When a whole view is loading.

accessibility: The text inside the spinner is its label. Name what is in progress, such as Loading runs. There is no spinner without text.
Set role="status" on the spinner so a screen reader announces the text when the app adds it.
When the text changes with each step, such as Cloning then Installing, keep one role="status" element in the page and change its text. Each change is announced.
Remove the spinner when the work ends. If it failed, put an error state or an alert in its place.
The mark is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup. It stops turning under prefers-reduced-motion, and the text still says what is happening.
A spinner is not focusable. An action that stops the work is a separate button beside it.

components.name: streaming
components.title: Streaming
components.purpose: The note that the agent is still producing output: a small turning mark and words that say what is happening.
whenToUse: As the last row of a transcript while a turn runs.
Beside a task's title or its Stop control, to say that work is still going on.
whenNotToUse: On a button whose action is running. Set aria-busy on the button, which draws its own mark.
For progress with a known amount done. Use a progress element.
To say that a turn has ended. Use a message of the turn-end kind.

variants.name: row
variants.use: On the last li of a transcript. It takes the padding of a message row, so the words line up with the labels above.

accessibility: Always write the words. The mark is drawn by the stylesheet and is not announced.

Put role="status" on the element that holds the words, so a screen reader announces them when they change. Keep that element in the page before the words change, and remove the indicator when the work ends.

Change the words only when the state changes, such as from working to stopping. Put figures that tick, such as elapsed time, in gw-streaming__detail outside the role="status" element, so they are not announced every second.
Under prefers-reduced-motion the mark stops turning and the words remain.
It holds no control and takes no focus. The app adds it when a turn starts and removes it when the turn ends.

components.name: tab-bar
components.title: Tab bar
components.purpose: The two to five main destinations of an app, along the bottom of a phone screen, each with an icon and a text label.
whenToUse: For moving between the top-level screens of an app on a phone.
When the app has two to five such screens and every one of them exists.
As the last element in the page, so it sits at the bottom of the screen.
whenNotToUse: At 768px and wider. The bar is not shown there, so list the same destinations in the app's sidebar.
For more than five destinations. Keep the five most used and put the rest behind a menu action in the app header.
For switching between panels inside one view. Use tabs.
For an action such as New task. A destination is a screen, so use a button in the view.
For going back from a screen below a destination. Use the back link in the app header.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 56px tall, with the destinations in equal columns across the full width. Shown only below 768px.

accessibility: Use a nav element with an aria-label, such as Main, holding one link per destination. They are links, not tabs, so they take no tab roles.
Set aria-current="page" on the link for the screen that is open, and on no other. It draws the mark and is what a screen reader announces.
Every link has a text label of one or two words. The icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
Tab moves through the destinations in order and Enter follows one. Both come from the link element.
The current destination is marked by a bar and a heavier label as well as by colour.
Keep the destinations in the same order on every screen.
The bar is sticky to the bottom of the page. Give the scrolling container scroll-padding-bottom of the bar's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.
When the bar and a sidebar are both in the markup, the one that is not shown is not in the accessibility tree, so the destinations are announced once.

components.name: textarea
components.title: Textarea
components.purpose: The multi-line control of a field, which grows with what the reader types.
whenToUse: For text that runs to more than one line: a prompt, review notes, a list of commands.
With the mono variant, for text a machine will read, such as commands or a prompt with code in it.
whenNotToUse: For one line of text, such as a name or a branch. Use a text input in a field.
To show text the reader never edits or copies. Write it as plain text.
Outside a field. The label, description and error come from the field.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Prose in the interface typeface. No modifier class.

variants.name: mono
variants.use: Commands, code and prompts where spacing and punctuation matter. Set spellcheck="false" with it.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: As wide as the field, 88px tall when empty, growing with its content to 264px and scrolling after that. Where the browser cannot grow it, it is 132px tall and the reader can drag it taller.

accessibility: Use a textarea element carrying both gw-field__control and gw-textarea, inside gw-field, with a label element whose for attribute matches its id.
State comes from the field control: aria-invalid="true" with a linked gw-field__error, the disabled attribute, or the readonly attribute.
Link the description, and the error while there is one, by listing their ids in aria-describedby.
Enter adds a line. It never submits the form, so the form needs a button for that.
Past its maximum height the control scrolls with the arrow keys and Page Up and Page Down, as any textarea does.
A read-only textarea stays focusable and its text can be selected and copied. A disabled one leaves the tab order.
